bug_semantics: An administrator can store a webhook URL and cause Ech0 to POST to that URL with a default http.Client that never inspects DNS-resolved addresses. CreateWebhook only rejected empty names/URLs. A later validateWebhookURL (webhook_setting_service.go) tried to block private targets but used net.ParseIP on the hostname, so literals such as 10.0.0.1 were rejected while hostnames such as 169.254.169.254.nip.io returned nil and passed. TestWebhook and the dispatcher then resolved those hostnames and requested cloud-metadata and other internal endpoints; delivery status leaked reachability.
flaw_origin: The SSRF mechanism is the unguarded outbound POST to an admin-supplied webhook URL. That first appeared in 3f7c5a6c885f01510762f695833ff7db8e67276f (internal/event/dispatcher.go): NewWebhookDispatcher installed &http.Client{Timeout: 5s} with no DialContext, and Dispatch called http.NewRequestWithContext(..., "POST", wh.URL, ...) plus client.Do. The parent left Dispatch empty. CreateWebhook already persisted arbitrary URLs. df4b49437762826b9ba9c8c9bbd6f673dcffd03b later added the ParseIP-only validator cited by GHSA-r2x7-427f-rq69; that is a failed mitigation of the original send path, not the first write of the request.
